summary: Isparta province stands under the national framework of Turkey. No Isparta-specific statute, incident, police action, court decision or facility practice appears in the sources behind this record, so the national assessment carried by the Turkey record applies here without local modification.
tangentialFactors: Bans and force against Pride participants are documented in other Turkish provinces rather than in Isparta: on 14 June 2019 the governors of Izmir, Antalya and Istanbul banned the 7th Izmir Pride, the 3rd Antalya Pride and the 27th Istanbul Pride, and in June 2025 authorities issued blanket bans against the Istanbul LGBTI and trans pride marches, with police using unlawful force and over 90 people arbitrarily detained. Isparta has no sourced Pride event, ban or dispersal of its own, so its absence from the record reflects the sourcing rather than a documented difference in local practice.
localsOnly: No Isparta-specific provision governing residents was identified: the province has no sourced local ordinance on gender markers, facilities, policing or healthcare access. Residents of Isparta hold the national position on legal gender recognition, military service and the absence of a comprehensive discrimination law, which is set out in the national record for Turkey.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether the three draft law packages targeting LGBTI people made public during 2025 were ever submitted to parliament is unresolved in the sources, as is the status of the February 2026 newspaper report that the government was considering a sentence of one to three years for publicly encouraging 'behavior contrary to biological sex'. The sources also leave unresolved whether the November 2025 court ruling that overturned the Istanbul governorate ban as disproportionate and unlawful affected the prosecutions of 92 people, which were continuing at year's end.

The inventory holds no Isparta-specific data on detention numbers, facility conditions, hate-crime outcomes or access to hormone therapy. Those questions are not sourced for this province rather than established as absent locally.
